name: Sea Thrift
blurb: Tight cushions of grassy leaves and round pom-pom blooms.
description: Sea thrift grows where little else will: cliff ledges, salt spray, thin gravelly soil. It forms neat evergreen tufts and sends up papery globe flowers from late spring into summer. Plant it along a path edge or tuck it into a rock wall.

name: Sweet Alyssum
blurb: Low clouds of tiny honey-scented white flowers.
description: The white froth you see spilling over coastal paths. Sweet alyssum flowers for months, smells faintly of honey and pulls in hoverflies and bees. Lovely at the front of a border or in a window box.

name: Coastal Sage
blurb: Soft silver-green leaves that shrug off wind and salt.
description: A hardy culinary sage selected for exposed gardens. Velvety leaves, purple-blue summer spikes and a compact habit that stays tidy in a pot. Pick leaves all year.

name: Lamb's Ear
blurb: Felted grey leaves you will want to touch every time.
description: Thick, woolly leaves form a silver mat that spreads slowly and suppresses weeds. A favourite with children and pollinators alike, and very forgiving in poor soil.

name: Beach Rose
blurb: Tough, fragrant and covered in big hips by autumn.
description: The classic dune rose. Crinkled leaves, single open flowers with a strong clove scent and tomato-red hips in autumn. Makes a dense, salt-proof hedge.

name: Bayberry
blurb: Aromatic leaves and waxy grey-blue winter berries.
description: A semi-evergreen shrub for sandy, salty sites. Crush a leaf for a clean resinous scent. Female plants carry clusters of waxy berries that birds love through winter.
